documents.title: Laura Brenner: apartment condition, June 11, 2016
documents.text:
From: Laura Brenner
To: Eleanor Whitcomb
Date: June 11, 2016
Subject: Apartment condition

Attached are photographs detailing the condition of the screens and other issues in the apartment, all of which were existing upon our arrival. I know you're aware of the terrace, the intercom/doorbell and perhaps others of these as well, but I've included everything that's not strictly cosmetic like the paint and wires. If you have questions about any of this please let me know.

Laura

22 photographs attached.

documents.title: Move-out walk-through, March 1, 2018
documents.text:
Move-out walk-through, March 1, 2018. Present: Eleanor Whitcomb (owner), Michael Brenner (tenant), Karen Liu (broker) and Paul Novak. Eleanor took 60 photographs; Paul recorded a video.
Entrance and stairs: front step chipped; saddle past the vestibule gouged with a broken corner; common-foyer mahogany door with veneer sheared off one section; newel post chipped and gouged; stair carpet edges scraped and torn on several steps; top molding and rail edge damaged between the second and third floors.
Living room: parquet scraped, scratched and gouged; decorative border missing inlay pieces and stained; finish worn through in places.
Dining room: paint blotches, gouges and a large stain on the parquet; damaged parquet corners; antique hearth tiles missing and broken; mahogany mantel damaged; a large piece of the doorway casing damaged or missing.
Office: carpet heavily stained; floor scratched. Mahogany window sills throughout: stains, ring marks and gouges.
West master suite: large dark stains on the plank floor, including in front of the fireplace, with a urine odor; scrapes and gouges; soot staining on the wall, ceiling, mantel and shelving; a deep gouge in the molding.
East master bedroom: ceiling damaged where the period chandeliers were replaced with the tenants' fixtures. East bathroom ceiling stained and damaged.
Third floor: southeast bedroom loft-ladder railing pulled away, with protruding nails and torn wood; not safe to use. Northeast storage-ladder railing scraped. Northeast bedroom plank floor with a dark urine stain; bedroom door broken and the plaster behind it damaged. Bathroom tub porcelain chipped and vanity panel broken. Great-room plank floor heavily stained and gouged with a urine odor; plaster damage and staining down one wall; ceiling damaged around the light fixtures.
Karen Liu also noted odors in several rooms.

documents.title: Lease, renewal and February 2018 modification
documents.text:
Residential lease, 142 West 88th Street, Triplex. Landlord: Whitcomb Holdings LLC. Tenants: Laura and Michael Brenner. Signed November 24, 2014. Initial term January 1, 2015 to June 30, 2016. Renewed April 8, 2016 through June 30, 2018. Modified February 12, 2018 to end on February 28, 2018. Security deposit held by landlord: $43,800.
Lease ¶31: Tenant has inspected the apartment and building, states they are in good order and repair, and takes the apartment as-is except for latent defects.
Rider ¶4: Tenant pays one half of the water and gas bills within 30 days of receiving copies from the landlord.
Rider ¶6: Tenant returns the apartment in its original condition, normal wear and tear excepted. Landlord may apply the security deposit to damage.
Rider ¶14: Tenant must inform landlord of any pre-existing damage within two days of occupancy.
Rider ¶39: Landlord permits the tenant's four existing dogs: two small mixed-breed dogs, one bulldog and one miniature dachshund. No additional pets without the landlord's prior permission.
Modification ¶8: Landlord and tenant walk through the apartment for damage within 48 hours of vacancy.

documents.title: Owner instructions
documents.text:
From Eleanor Whitcomb, March 2, 2018.
I want the triplex back on the market as soon as possible, ideally showing in May for a summer move-in.
Have Feld Architecture walk the apartment first and give me a condition schedule and a scope with a budget before we commit to repairs. Then line up the trades.
The loft-ladder railing is dangerous. Keep everyone off that ladder until it is fixed.
The kitchen water repair is a separate job Feld is already handling. Keep it out of this.
You can approve work within the funds I've set aside; I don't need to sign each contract. Deal with the contractors directly.
I'll settle the Brenners' deposit separately once we know what the damage costs.

documents.title: Feld Architecture: restoration assessment
documents.text: Feld Architecture offers a restoration assessment of the triplex. One site visit of up to three hours. We produce a room-by-room condition schedule with photographs and measurements, a written scope of repairs with a preliminary budget, and flag any immediate safety issues. Fixed fee: site assessment $600; condition and quantity schedule $300; scope and budget note $300; total $1,200 including travel. Earliest visit Monday, March 5. Report within two business days of the visit. Invoice on delivery of the report, payable within 14 days. Kitchen water work is covered under our separate engagement and is excluded. Offer valid through March 31, 2018.

documents.title: Condition and maintenance history
documents.text:
Condition and maintenance history, compiled by Eleanor Whitcomb.
Before the tenancy: the apartment was painted and the floors redone in late 2014. Karen Liu's 2014 listing photographs show intact fireplace tiles and window woodwork, and good floors with a few dark spots and one diagonal scratch in the living room. A family stayed briefly over the 2014 holidays before the Brenners moved in on January 9, 2015.
June 11, 2016: Laura Brenner emailed 22 photographs of screens, a loose dining-room hearth, loose or broken tiles, missing molding and a small missing parquet piece, describing them as existing on arrival. None of this was reported within the two days required by rider ¶14.
Complaints during the tenancy: uneven room temperatures, a clogged toilet, a roof leak, weak dryer performance, bin lids and the intercom. Work done: screens repaired, window weather stripping and five temperature sensors added, a new intercom installed and the leaks repaired.
June 2016: during a screen inspection Eleanor found a dog accident on the floor; Laura apologized and cleaned it up.
Repeated indoor grilling caused grease odors and set off smoke alarms. Eleanor asked the Brenners to stop.
January 2018: Feld Architecture was hired about water in the kitchen. That repair is separate from the move-out work.

documents.title: Westside Plaster & Paint: plaster, paint and woodwork
documents.text: Westside Plaster & Paint: plaster repair and soot cleanup in the great room, northeast bedroom and west master suite: $11,366.67. Paint walls, ceilings and trim throughout, including ceiling repairs at the light fixtures: $12,783.32. Restore woodwork and fireplaces: window sills, doorway casing, moldings, mantels, hearth tiles, foyer door veneer and the northeast bedroom door: $10,000. Bathroom repairs and caulking: tub chip repair and vanity panel: $3,762.50. Total $37,912.49. Deposit of $10,000 at start; balance on completion, payable within 14 days. About two weeks on site. Earliest start March 12. Offer valid through April 30, 2018.

workPlan.title: Immediate make-safe + restoration assessment (kitchen water repair excluded)
workPlan.summary: Proceed with (1) immediate make-safe repair of the unsafe loft-ladder railing, and (2) Feld Architecture’s move-out restoration assessment deliverables (site visit + condition/quantity schedule + scope/budget note) to define and sequence the broader restoration work. This keeps the kitchen water repair separate and allows trades to be lined up efficiently afterward.
workPlan.desiredOutcome: Make the triplex safe to access/market and obtain a bid-ready move-out restoration scope/budget (excluding kitchen water repair) so we can select and schedule the right repair trades within the $65,000 restoration set-aside.
scope: Rebuild and secure the southeast bedroom loft-ladder railing to make it safe; remove/secure protruding nails and reattach/repair torn wood as needed.
Site visit to inspect move-out restoration conditions throughout the triplex; document observed deficiencies (excluding kitchen water repair).
Produce a room-by-room condition and quantity schedule for move-out restoration items observed around 2018-03-01 (excluding kitchen water repair).
Deliver a written scope note and preliminary budget for move-out restoration, with explicit exclusion of the kitchen water repair job.
fixedRequirements: Keep the kitchen water repair separate from the move-out restoration.
workPlan.rationale: 1) Safety: the SE bedroom loft-ladder railing is documented as pulled away with protruding nails and explicitly called out as unsafe; access notes say to keep off that ladder until repaired. 2) Sequencing: owner instruction is to have Feld Architecture walk first and produce a condition schedule and scope/budget before committing to broader repairs. 3) Separation: Feld’s quote and owner instruction both exclude kitchen water repair; this proposal maintains that separation.
